title: Split digraphs a_e, i_e, o_e, u_e
examples: Teacher, what is the magic e doing to the word cap?
When do I know to add the magic e to a word?

explain.say: Listen carefully to this word. It is cap. Say cap aloud for me.

draw.text: Split digraphs a_e, i_e, o_e, u_e

explain.say: Now I am going to add a magic e to the end. The word becomes cape. Say cape aloud for me.
Did you notice how the 'a' sound changed? It made a long 'a' sound. This is the magic e at work.
When we read, the silent e makes the vowel say its name. This is the rule we are learning today.

items: silent e makes vowel say name

explain.say: Let us try another word. If we have hop, adding the magic e makes hope. Say hope for me.

faq.q: Why is the 'e' silent in these words?
faq.a: The magic e does not make a sound when you read it. It just helps the vowel next to it say its full name.
asks: Does the e make any sound?

faq.q: Does this happen with all vowels?
faq.a: Yes, this pattern works for all five vowels: a, e, i, o, and u. You must add the e to make the change.
asks: Can I use this with every letter?

faq.q: If I write it, do I always add the e?
faq.a: When you are spelling, you must remember to write the silent e to get the long vowel sound. It is a spelling rule.
asks: Do I always write the e?

faq.q: What is the difference between reading and spelling this?
faq.a: When reading, you just hear the long sound. When spelling, you must write the magic e to make that long sound.
asks: How is reading different from writing?
Do I sound it out or write it?

faq.q: Can I use this rule with two vowels together?
faq.a: This rule is for one vowel followed by a silent e. Two vowels together usually make a different sound pattern.
asks: Does this work with two vowels?

facts: The magic e is also called the silent e.
It makes the vowel before it say its long sound.
For example, 'kit' becomes 'kite' with the magic e.
This pattern helps us read and spell long vowel sounds.

quiz.say: What is the long sound in 'make'?
quiz.why: The magic e makes the short 'a' sound change to a long 'a' sound.

wrong.1: This is tempting because 'cap' has a short 'a' sound.
wrong.2: This is wrong because the vowel sound is 'a', not 'e'.
wrong.3: This is wrong because the 'e' is silent, but the 'a' sound changes.

quiz.say: If you write 'hop' but want the long 'o' sound, what do you add?
quiz.why: You must add the silent 'e' to change the short 'o' sound to a long 'o' sound.

wrong.1: Adding 'a' would change the sound to something else entirely.
wrong.2: Adding 'i' does not follow the magic e rule for the 'o' vowel.
wrong.3: Adding another vowel does not create the necessary long sound.

quiz.say: Which word correctly shows the long 'i' sound?
quiz.why: The word 'site' uses the magic e to make the 'i' say its name.

wrong.0: This is not a real word and does not follow the spelling rule.
wrong.1: Adding 'a' changes the vowel sound completely.
wrong.3: This word has a short 'i' sound, not the long 'i' sound.
